summary: Section 3.3's lifted atlas is landed in vendor/truck/truck-certified/src/kernel/atlas.rs and wired through kernel/mod.rs: pub struct ChartAtlas over a rational carrier holding the FINITE chart family per carrier kind (chart ids, certified-regular regions, ChartLattice deck generators, ChartPatch CertifiedPatch leaves, and the pole/partner switch data). The sphere atlas is the pole-chart family (two rationalized polar half-angle pole charts degenerate on the polar line u = 0 through u = v = 0, plus their stereographic partners that are regular AT the same pole), with the exact rational pole-to-partner transition (point map pole_to_partner and its outward-rounded box transport pole_to_partner_box). Cone and Torus join the admitted carrier family here: ChartAtlas::try_new accepts them and constructs their chart families (the cone's apex-excluding charts keep the carrier-singularity apex locus; the torus builds the product-of-half-angle family), while the Wave-1 404 pending refusal in kernel::rational is preserved untouched (the re-route is asserted in tests/kernel_atlas.rs, never by editing the landed files). Section 3.4's doctrine is code: classify_degeneracy(p: &dyn CertifiedPatch, box_) over one of the atlas's own chart patches returns DegeneracyRoute::{SwitchChart{target}, CarrierSingular} - the sphere pole box (rank-deficient parameterization at a regular image point, partner regularity Proven over its pole box) routes SwitchChart and the arc continues with no valence change; the cone apex box (a genuine carrier singularity, no partner) routes CarrierSingular. K2 lifts run through the atlas: Param is the LIFTED coordinate (5.9 stays 5.9; the deck integer carries the winding), the unwrapped pcurve run 5.9 -> 6.4 lifts to deck +1 with canonical u = 6.4 - P (the shim kit deck-wrap fixture), and |deck| > DECK_MAX on one edge refuses RefusalKind::DeckExhausted (Inconclusive). N4 is pinned by the module's source test: no sin/cos/atan2/exp/ln/log/powf/sqrt call in atlas.rs; H-1 discipline holds (no unwrap/expect/panic!, no module-level allow).

measured_counts.sphere_pole_chart_region_regularity: Proven (EG-F^2 = 64 u^2 / ((1+u^2)^4 (1+v^2)^2) lower bound positive on the region u in [0.5,2], v in [-1.5,1.5])
measured_counts.pole_to_partner_transition_checks: agrees with the direct partner coordinates to < 1e-12 on all pre-pole samples
measured_counts.cone_chart_family: 2 apex-excluding half-angle sheets, each region axial lower bound 0.1 (> 0, apex at v = 0 excluded)

design_notes.classify_degeneracy: implemented as ChartAtlas::classify_degeneracy(&self, p: &dyn CertifiedPatch, box_) because the SwitchChart target and the 'image certified regular elsewhere' premise need the atlas's partner charts; p must be one of the atlas's own Chart::patch leaves (matched by object address). An out-of-atlas CertifiedPatch routes CarrierSingular (refuse/trim).
design_notes.pole_chart_geometry: the sphere pole charts are the rationalized polar half-angle charts (u = tan(theta/2), v = tan(phi/2)); their u = 0 polar line collapses onto the pole u = v = 0. The partner stereographic charts are regular at that same pole, so classify certifies the pole image regular elsewhere and routes SwitchChart.
design_notes.cone_and_torus_leaves: the cone/torus CertifiedPatch leaves keep the crate's deferred pending markers (cone_half_angle_slope_needs_data / torus_rational_form_pending) - an exactly rational slope cannot be recovered N4-cleanly from a stored half-angle, and the torus enclosure machinery is later work. This packet certifies the CHART structure (ids, regions, apex-excluding boxes, lattice) and the section 3.4 routing over it; the Wave-1 kernel::rational refusal surface is untouched.
design_notes.transitions: exact affine/rational data with outward-rounded transport (CertifiedInterval map for the box form); no transcendental transition is needed for any admitted carrier (stop condition 2 not triggered).
design_notes.chart_switch_breaks: a pole switch is a SegmentBreak::ChartSwitch, not a topology node; the pole crossing adds no valence because the partner certifies the crossing point regular.
